summary: Console impersonation failing after auth-proxy cookie-prefix change
description: Issue summary: After a recent auth-proxy rollout that normalized cookie prefixes, the Console 'Run as user' / impersonation flow intermittently returns 403 for support engineers and oncall. Impact: prevents support from performing oncall troubleshooting or using impersonation runbooks for customer investigations. Not a complete outage but significantly impairs oncall response.
impact: Support engineers report 20-30% failure rate for impersonation attempts in us-west; delays in oncall escalations and a missed pager escalation window for one incident.
steps_to_reproduce: 2) From support tools, select a target user and click 'Impersonate / Run as'.
3) Console attempts token exchange with auth-proxy and then calls service-ticket endpoint.
4) Observe immediate 403 response and console shows 'Impersonation denied: session mismatch'.
5) Repeating the flow in same session sometimes succeeds (racey), other times fails consistently until app restart.
6) Reproduction more reliable when user agent is Electron (desktop) and less frequent from browser.
observed_behavior: 403 returned from /internal/v1/impersonate with log 'cookie validation failed: multiple session cookies; prefix mismatch'. Electron session shows stale cookie present with __Host- and without- prefix variants.
expected_behavior: Impersonation flow should succeed when user has valid session and support has privileges; cookie normalization should be transparent to downstream services.
logs: 2026-03-12T17:08:12Z auth-proxy[proxy-23] WARN cookie_validator: found duplicate session cookies: session, __Host-session; choosing longest path -> validation failed
2026-03-12T17:08:12Z console-service[runas] ERROR token_exchange: external 403 from auth-proxy (reason=CookiePrefixMismatch)
2026-03-12T17:09:55Z electron-client[desktop-71] DEBUG cookie-store: retained legacy 'session' cookie alongside new '__Host-session' after proxy set-cookie response
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): replicated in prod us-west with Electron client; browser repros much less frequent.
SRE looked at recent auth-proxy change: PR #2345 added stricter '__Host-' prefix enforcement for cookies to tighten path/scoping.

Hypothesis: proxy now issues __Host-session but older Electron client keeps non-prefixed session cookie, causing validation to detect duplicate cookies and treat as potential session-splitting attack -> rejects request.

Observed that cookie path and domain differ slightly for legacy cookie (path=/; domain=.redwood.internal) vs __Host- cookie (path=/; no domain attr) — srv-side validator treats this as two active session cookies.

Temporary mitigation tested: proxy added a normalization header that instructs Electron client to delete legacy cookie on next response; immediate drop in 403s for users who received the normalization header.
Related deploys: auth-proxy rollout v2.1.8 (2026-03-11) referenced in Slack #deploys and linked PR.
Edge case: support-runbooks that use embedded webviews (electron) do not clear legacy cookie automatically; persists across app restarts for some users due to client-side cookie store bug.
Risk: rolling back proxy change reduces the enforcement benefit; client upgrade plus norm header preferred.

SRE - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-12): Confirmed cookie prefix change on 2026-03-11. Hypothesis: duplicate cookies trigger validator rejection. Will try normalization header as low-risk mitigation.
Reporter - Maya Chen (2026-03-12): Verified workaround after Liam applied normalization header to proxy in us-west canary: impersonation attempts succeeded for 7/8 previously failing sessions.

Desktop Eng - Nora Patel (2026-03-13): Electron client has known cookie-store TTL issue; will push an update (PR referenced) to explicitly remove legacy 'session' cookie when encountering __Host- variant.
SRE - Liam O'Connor (2026-03-13): Patch deployed to production us-west: normalization header active for 1 hour; monitoring shows error rate for impersonation dropped from 26% to 3%.
Support Triage - Priya S. (2026-03-13): Marking as 'In Progress' while Desktop ENG completes client publish and we monitor long-tail failures. Notifying oncall and internal access docs.
workaround: Temporary proxy normalization header added to instruct clients to delete legacy 'session' cookie; effective immediately in us-west. Desktop client patch queued and will be rolled out in electron v3.4.1.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied (normalization header) and desktop client patch in flight. Plan: 1) ship electron client fix to explicitly remove legacy cookie (PR merged), 2) keep normalization header for 48h post-client rollout, 3) monitor impersonation success rate and then remove normalization header. Final resolution will include postmortem and runbook update.
next_steps: Desktop ENG to merge and ship electron v3.4.1 with explicit legacy-cookie removal (ETA 2026-03-15).
SRE to leave normalization header enabled in us-west until client uptake >= 95% (monitoring dashboard link in confluence).
Support to update internal runbook 'Impersonation troubleshooting' with note about cookie-prefix migration and temporary remediation steps.
Conduct short postmortem after full rollout and create a preventative ticket to add cookie-compatibility tests to CI for proxy changes.
